front: Name the 6 kinds of grouse you can hunt in BC.
back: Ruffed, spruce, dusky (Interior), sooty (coast), sharp tailed, and ptarmigan (3 kinds). (85%)

front: Ruffed grouse: male or female? Unbroken tail band, 2 rump dots.
back: Male. Hen: band broken in the middle, 1 rump dot. Use two clues. (70 to 85%)

front: Ruffed grouse: middle tail feather length for a male?
back: About 15 cm (6 in) or more. Under 14 cm (5.5 in): female. In between: use another clue. (70%)

front: Young of the year or adult: which feathers do you check?
back: The 2 outer flight feathers, P9 and P10. Pointed and frayed: young. Rounded: adult. (85%)

front: P9 or P10 still growing in. Young or adult?
back: Adult. Young birds do not moult P9 and P10 in their first summer. (85%)

front: Spruce grouse male: 3 marks.
back: Black throat and breast edged white, red comb over the eye, black tail. Franklin's form: white spots above the tail. (80 to 85%)

front: Why is the spruce grouse called the fool hen?
back: It trusts its camouflage and often lets people walk close. (80%)

front: Sooty vs dusky grouse: where?
back: Sooty: wet coast forest (Region 2 lists SOOTY (Blue)). Dusky: drier Interior (Regions 3 and 8 list DUSKY (Blue)). One species, blue grouse, until 2006. (85 to 99%)

front: Dusky grouse weight range?
back: About 880 g to 1.6 kg: the biggest forest grouse in BC. (80%)

front: Smallest grouse?
back: White tailed ptarmigan, about 350 g. (85%)

front: Sharp tailed grouse: 3 field marks.
back: Pale with V marks on a white breast, short pointed tail with longer middle feathers, white in flight. (80 to 85%)

front: Sharp tailed grouse in BC: how many, and status?
back: About 10,000 breeding birds (2001). Columbian subspecies on the provincial Blue List. (85%)

front: Where are sharp tailed grouse open in Region 3?
back: Only MUs 3-30 and 3-31, 10 Sept to 30 Nov, 5 (10). Not the part of 3-30 south of the Scottie Creek FSR, Map C18. (99%)

front: Which ptarmigan has a white tail all year?
back: White tailed ptarmigan. Willow and rock keep black tails. (85%)

front: Ptarmigan feet?
back: Feathered: unique among chicken like birds, they work like snowshoes. (85%)

front: Sage grouse in BC: season?
back: None. No season row anywhere in the synopsis. (90%, my reading)

front: Ptarmigan or sharp tailed grouse in Region 8?
back: No row for either in Region 8. (99%)

front: Why is grouse breast white meat?
back: Fast muscle fibres that run on stored sugar: big power for a few seconds, then they tire. (70%)

front: What is the keel?
back: The blade on the breastbone that anchors the big flight muscles. (80%)

front: How does air move through a bird's lung?
back: One way, pushed by air sacs that act as bellows. The lung is rigid. (80%)

front: How many air sacs do most birds have?
back: About 9, in a front set and a rear set. (70%)

front: Where are a grouse's heart and lungs?
back: Lungs high against the back; heart low and forward under the front breast. (80%)

front: Grouse body temperature?
back: About 41.5 C (40.4 to 42.6 C in captive ruffed grouse). (75%)

front: Crop, gizzard, ceca: one job each.
back: Crop stores, gizzard grinds with grit, ceca ferment fibre. (80%)

front: Why do grouse pick gravel?
back: Grit for the gizzard to grind buds, seeds and needles. (85%)

front: Spruce grouse winter diet?
back: Up to 99% conifer needles once snow covers the ground. Gut grows about 40% longer. (75%)

front: Favourite winter food of ruffed grouse?
back: Aspen flower buds. They avoid birch and alder catkins when they can choose. (80%)

front: How warm is a snow roost?
back: Under 20 cm of soft snow: -3 to -12 C while the air was as low as -35 C. (75%)

front: What are pectinations?
back: Comb like scales on a grouse's toes in winter: snowshoes. (85%)

front: Ruffed grouse chick survival?
back: Over 3 in 4 die within 35 days, most in the first week. (75%)

front: Adult ruffed grouse yearly survival?
back: About 1 in 2 (Pennsylvania). Hardest months: January to March. (75%)

front: Why open the crop of a shot grouse?
back: It shows what they eat right now. Hunt that food. (Tip)

front: Grouse field of view?
back: About 300 degrees; only about 30 degrees with both eyes (chicken data, 75%). Blind spot straight behind.

front: Do grouse see colour?
back: Yes: four cone types (violet, blue, green, red), one more than us (75%, chicken data). They key on motion.

front: Do grouse smell hunters?
back: No study found that they do. Wind matters for sound and your dog's nose. (Tip)

front: What sounds carry to a grouse?
back: Low thumps: boots on rock, truck doors, voices. Their inner ear is tuned low. (65%; Tip)

front: Grouse escape plan in 5 steps?
back: Freeze, walk off under cover, flush with a roar, glide under about 90 m, land in a tree and freeze again. (75 to 80%)

front: Why does stopping make grouse flush?
back: Hunter lore: a stopped predator may have seen it. Be ready when you stop. (Tip)

front: How do you work a dog on grouse?
back: Into the wind, so it meets the scent cone drifting downwind. (Tip)

front: Body language: about to flush?
back: Neck stretched tall, crest up, tail fanning. (Tip, hunter lore)

front: Harvest rate near open roads vs farther away (Pennsylvania)?
back: 48% near open roads, 19% farther. (75%)

front: Male survival within vs beyond 201 m of roads?
back: 23% within, 36% beyond. Walk past the road band. (75%)

front: When do ruffed grouse families break up?
back: At about 12 weeks, early fall. (75%)

front: How far do young ruffed grouse disperse?
back: Young hens about 4.8 km, young males about 2.1 km, over 2 to 3 weeks (Wisconsin). (80%)

front: Adults share of the bag: October vs December?
back: 34% in October, 57% in December (Pennsylvania). (75%)

front: A grouse flushes and glides into a fir. What now?
back: Mark the tree and walk straight to it, ready for a second flush. (Tip)

front: Bird disappears under a lone evergreen?
back: Circle the tree: it may walk out and flush from the far side. (Tip)

front: Hen ruffed grouse with chicks: what does she do?
back: Hisses, fans tail and ruff, may fake a broken wing to lead you away. (70%)

front: How does a ruffed grouse drum?
back: Stands on a log and beats cupped wings against the air. The wings never hit the log. (85%)

front: When do ruffed grouse drum most?
back: Spring, March to May; peak in April in one study. A little in fall too. (75 to 85%)

front: How far can you hear a drum?
back: About 400 m or more in thick woods, depending which way the bird faces. (60 to 70%)

front: Dusky grouse display?
back: Deep hoots with neck air sacs showing (reddish purple), yellow orange comb. Heard up to about 400 m. (75%)

front: Spruce grouse display?
back: Struts with red combs up and tail fanned; short flight ending in two loud wing claps. (65 to 75%)

front: Sharp tailed grouse display?
back: Dawn dance on a lek: stamping feet, rattling tail, pink neck sacs. Lek calls carry up to 1.5 km. (85%)

front: Ruffed grouse clutch and incubation?
back: 7 to 12 eggs, 23 to 24 days, hatch usually early June. (85%)

front: Sharp tailed grouse average clutch in BC?
back: 12.8 eggs. First clutch at 11 months. (85%)

front: When do ruffed grouse chicks fly well?
back: Short hops in week 1, fly well by week 3. (75%)

front: What do dusky grouse do in fall?
back: Move uphill into dense conifers and eat needles all winter: an upside down migration. (70 to 75%)

front: When are ptarmigan white?
back: Mostly white by mid October. (85%)

front: Region 3 grouse seasons (MUs 3-12 to 3-20, 3-26 to 3-44)?
back: Youth only 1 to 9 Sept; general 10 Sept to 30 Nov. (99%)

front: Region 2 grouse season?
back: Bow only 1 to 9 Sept; general 10 Sept to 15 Dec, MUs 2-2 to 2-19. (99%)

front: Region 8 grouse seasons?
back: Youth 1 to 9 Sept; general 10 Sept to 30 Nov; bow only 1 to 10 Dec. (99%)

front: Legal hunting hours for grouse?
back: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset (item 38). Ducks are 30 minutes. (99%)

front: A grouse day in 4 parts?
back: Feed and grit at dawn, rest and dust midday, feed late day, roost at night. (hunter lore, 75%)

front: Best time for the .22 still hunt?
back: Midday, when spruce and dusky grouse sit in trees. (Tip)

front: Grouse on a windy day?
back: Wild and skittish; hunt sheltered draws and thick cover. (Tip, hunter lore)

front: Grouse on a rainy day?
back: Under thick conifers. (Tip, hunter lore)

front: Grouse and the moon or pressure fronts?
back: No grouse study found. Do not plan around them; log your own data. (VERIFY)

front: Ruffed grouse elevation band in BC?
back: Most abundant 750 to 1,250 m, aspen and poplar near water. (85%)

front: Ruffed grouse forest age?
back: Young forest under about 20 years old. (75%)

front: Dusky grouse elevations in BC?
back: Many seen at 1,500 to 2,250 m; breeding at 500 to 1,250 m is not uncommon. (85%)

front: White tailed ptarmigan breeding height in the Interior?
Sharp tailed grouse key BC foods?
back: Snowberry, rose, dandelion; buds of water birch, aspen, saskatoon, chokecherry. (85%)

front: Ptarmigan winter food?
back: Willow, alder and dwarf birch buds and twigs. (85%)

front: Hunt Map: 4 steps for grouse ground?
back: Management Units and Forest Service roads; Cutblocks by age and Burns; Slope direction and Sun and shade; Elevation profile. (Tip)

front: Grouse near Heffley Creek, MU 3-27?
back: Ruffed, spruce, dusky, and ptarmigan up high. No sharp tailed season in 3-27. (90 to 99%)

front: Grouse in the South Okanagan (Region 8)?
back: Ruffed, spruce, dusky. 5 a day in total. No sharp tail, no ptarmigan. (99%)

front: Sun Peaks rule?
back: No hunting or shooting within 400 m of any lift, run, facility or development, MU 3-27, Map C11. (99%)

front: Grouse track?
back: About 5 cm: 3 long toes forward, 1 short back, in one zig zag line. (75%)

front: Normal grouse droppings?
back: Curved, fibrous, pencil thick, white tipped, 2.5 to 4 cm. (70 to 85%)

front: Caecal droppings: fresh or old?
back: Green is fresh; they turn black quickly. (65%)

front: Pile of droppings on one spot of a mossy log?
back: A ruffed grouse drum stand. He lives there year round. (85%)

front: Snow hole with wing marks beside it?
back: The grouse burst out and left. A hole with no exit sign may still hold a bird. (75%; Tip)

front: Dust bowl?
back: A shallow scrape in dry dirt with a few feathers, often on road edges. (80%)

front: Fresh track line heading into cover?
back: Slow down, walk beside the line, be ready. The bird is often within 50 m. (Tip)

front: Is a .22 rimfire legal for grouse?
back: Yes. Rimfire: grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only (page 13, note 2). Not quail, pheasant or partridge. (99%)

front: .22 on grouse: aim point and range?
back: Head or upper neck, inside about 25 m (27 yd), rested, dirt behind. (Tip)

front: .22 backstop rule of thumb?
back: Dirt behind the bird or no shot. A .22 bullet can fly over 1 km. (Tip; safety)

front: 400 m single projectile ban and your .22?
back: On listed highways (for example Hwy 5, Hope to Kamloops) no bullet within 400 m of the road allowance; shotgun with shot allowed. Hwy 5 north of Kamloops is not listed (95%). (99%)

front: Shotgun load for ruffed grouse?
back: 12 gauge, lead No. 7.5 or 6, improved cylinder. Lead is legal for upland birds. (Tip 60%; legal 99%)

front: Swing on a flushing grouse?
back: Bead behind, swing through past the beak, shoot, keep moving. Sky behind, nobody in front. (Tip)

front: Dogs on grouse: legal?
back: Yes, unleashed for small game. Training on game birds under supervision 1 Aug to 30 Apr. (99%)

front: Road allowance width on a road under 3 lanes?
back: 15 m either side of the middle, or to private or cultivated land if closer. (99%)

front: Which roads does the road allowance rule name?
back: Numbered highways and two lane or wider public roads kept by Transportation and Infrastructure, its contractors, the federal government or another province or territory. (99%)

front: Forest Service roads and the road allowance rule?
back: Wording does not clearly name FSRs: VERIFY with a conservation officer (70%). Items 22 and 28 still apply. Same safe habit. (99% for items)

front: Items 22 and 28 in one line?
back: No hunting from a motor vehicle; no live round in the chamber or attached magazine in or on any vehicle. (99%)

front: ATV on a Forest Service Road needs?
back: Valid driver's licence and at least $200,000 third party liability insurance. (99%)

front: Region 3 above 1,700 m: vehicles?
back: Motor vehicles except snowmobiles only on existing roads and trails. (99%)

front: Late season sharp tailed grouse?
back: Big flocks flush far; one chance. A modified choke helps. (60%)

front: What does an old hand do differently?
back: Hunts edges slowly, walks away from roads, marks every flush, circles evergreens, opens crops, keeps a log. (opinion)

front: What stays attached to a grouse until home?
back: One feathered wing (page 15). (99%)

front: Edible portions of a game bird?
back: Both breasts. They must go home, to a meat cutter or cold storage. (99%)

front: Upland bird possession limit?
back: 3 times the daily limit while hunting or going home; sharp tailed grouse in Region 3: 2 times. (99%)

front: Region 3 grouse daily bag?
back: 5 of each kind, 10 total a day, 30 in possession. (99%)

front: Region 8 grouse daily bag?
back: 5 total a day, 15 in possession. (99%)

front: Region 2 grouse daily bag?
back: 10 a day, 30 in possession (sooty, ruffed, spruce together). (99%)

front: Region 3 ptarmigan?
Field care in 4 words each?
back: Note species, wing on. Crop and guts out. Spread in shade. Cooler on ice. (80%)

front: Cool to what, cook to what?
back: Keep under 4 C; cook game birds to 74 C (165 F). (80%)

front: Fridge and freezer times for game birds?
back: Fridge up to 3 days; freezer up to 6 months. (80%)

front: A shot bird falls into brush. What do you do?
back: Eyes on the spot, pick a mark, walk straight there, search in growing circles. (Tip)
